title: Fibrewise flatness of an unramified smooth chart
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, n,c natural numbers, f_j in P=R[x_1,...,x_n], J=(f_j) and C=P/J [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Assume C is smooth over R [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and J/J^2 has a C-basis indexed by Fin c. For every g in D=C[y_1,...,y_c] and every R-algebra map theta:P -> D_g [def-weil-ring-localization-away], if D_g is formally unramified over P through theta [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], then it is flat over P through that same theta [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No prescribed values for the conormal basis or theta are assumed.

proof.text: The split conormal injection and the given rank-c basis identify Omega(C/R) plus C^c with C^n. Polynomial extension and localization give smoothness of B=D_g over R and rank n for Omega(B/R) at every prime. This uses the same split injection of Mathlib FormallySmooth.iff_split_injection, without the principal-localization conormal lemma.

proof.text: For a residue field k of R put T=B tensor_R k. Smoothness and differentials commute with base change, so T is smooth over k with differential rank n. Formal unramifiedness of P -> B also survives base change to k[z] -> T. At a maximal m of T, its contraction p in k[z] is maximal by Zariski lemma: the image k[z]/p is a finite-dimensional domain inside T/m. The two local rings are regular of dimension n, using the smooth differential-rank and closed-point dimension results.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH, corrected coordinates, Nakayama localization and fibrewise flatness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH

proof.text: The unramified fibre over p is a finite product of finite separable fields. Its localization at m is a field, so T_m/p T_m has dimension zero. The regular local target has depth at least n because its maximal ideal generators form a regular sequence. Miracle flatness gives flatness of k[z]_p -> T_m. Localizing from maximal to arbitrary primes and applying the local flatness criterion makes T flat over k[z].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07CH, corrected coordinates, Nakayama localization and fibrewise flatness; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CH

proof.text: At Q in Spec B with contractions q in P and p in R, use the fibrewise flatness criterion on R_p -> P_q -> B_Q with M=B_Q. The rings are localizations of finitely presented R_p-algebras; M is finite free of rank one over B_Q and nonzero. Smoothness of B over R gives R_p-flatness. The closed fibre map is a localization of the flat k[z] -> T. Thus B_Q is P_q-flat. The local flatness criterion proves flatness through theta globally.
